It's a virtual table with virtual assets that can be quite easily customized. A great platform for boardgame development, playtesting and virtual play. It doesn't hold your hand though. Its a bit quirky and dated by now, but it just works and that's just what we need.

Tabletop Simulator is more of a Workshop based game than the game itself, but the Workshop opens up many possibilities, as any individual is able to mod the game to make any board game in the world and upload it to share with the community. The game can be a bit buggy, laggy, and glitchy, but that can be expected as it is an early access game.

However, this game is probably not worth purchasing if you are not a board game fan. Also, it would probably be wise to purchase this game along with a few other friends, or if several of your friends already have it, so that you have people you can play it with. I've never got on a random server to try and play a game, but I've heard from other people that people on them can be trolls, which would ruin your experience and change your oppinion of the game itself.

This game has made it so much easier to play the games I grew up with without hunting them down on eBay for stupid amounts of money. I play 40k, my sister's special Star Wars edition of RISK, MTG, CAH and so many others. It's especially good since I'm so far away from my friends, we can still play and have a great time. Graphics are good, not amazing. The value in this game is in the Workshop integration and all the contributors putting all this free content online for everyone to enjoy. Totally worth the $20 any day of the week.

Tabletop Simulator combines the potential inherent in a physics-based sandbox with a wide combination of out-of-the-box board games and easily-subscribed Steam Workshop games. The controls are fun and easy to get the hang of, and you'll need them for everything from Dungeons & Dragons to Axis & Allies to five-player chess .

This is a wise investment even if you don't have many friends interested in tabletop games. Although it's generally a better experience with friends, meeting strangers and playing games with them is fun enough.

(Laser Light Show is a bitch though.)

The vanilla game isn't nearly worth the (non-sale) price. However, there is an extremely large modding community, which has created renditions of most real-life board games, so in practice the price you're paying is for the access to that specific library of mods. And I really mean it - modders have tirelessly (and probably with violation of multiple IP rights) transcribed TONS of board games from their paper form into their Tabletop Simulator versions. For that alone, TTS is a nice title to have in your library. Just a word of warning - while there are games intended for singleplayer, 99% will require at least one or two friends to play with. Not everyone has that luxury, so just keep that in mind.

Chances are, if you're looking at this game, you might be thinking of playing with friends. In that case, I heartily recommend this game for you. If you're thinking about solo play be warned - there are no AI or bots, any singleplayer game can be played just fine, but anything multiplayer requries actual people to play against. If you're looking at this with the hopes of completing it, i'd advise against it. Overall, it's a solid game, a great tool for playing games with friends, but is a little on the barer side when it comes to single-player features.

I see Tabletop Simulator not as a game, but rather, as a platform that allows you to play many board games. If you want to try new board games, you can go to Steam Workshop and download community-made board game mods for free. After that, you can immediately play that board game on Tabletop Simulator.

This is especially useful if you want to try new board game but that board game is not yet available in your region or when you are not sure whether a board game is worth buying or not.

Tabletop Simulator also shines in this COVID-19 quarantine period where you can't meet up with your friends to play physical board games. There is no reason not to play board game just because you and your friends stuck at home,

If you love board games, Tabletop Simulator is a must-buy item.

Alright, so I've been playing Tabletop Simulator for a while now, and I gotta say, this game is a blast! If you're into tabletop games or just want to have some fun with friends, this is the place to be.

The game is all about giving you the freedom to play and create your own tabletop games in a multiplayer physics sandbox. It's super cool how you can interact with the game pieces, move them around, and even customize the tables to create something entirely new.

There are some classic games included, like chess, checkers, and poker, but honestly, the magic happens when you start exploring the Steam Workshop. There are over 3,000 games and custom assets shared there, and you can even import your own images and models to create new pieces and tables.

The physics in the game are pretty solid too, so it feels like you're really moving pieces around on a table. Plus, you can play online with up to ten friends, which makes for some great game nights!

So, if you're a fan of board games or just like to mess around with physics, definitely give Tabletop Simulator a try. It's a solid pick for anyone who loves a good tabletop experience. Just be ready to lose hours of your life to this addictive sandbox!

1000 hours and countless adventures later, here we are. As a DM, I can say this is totally worth it. Other virtual table tops may be vastly more efficient but this captures the feeling of a home game the best, hands down. The jank of being negligent and letting your table get messy is part of the experience. It gets messy like your home table does, or as clean and well oiled as your home table does. You can decorate, put out candles, hell my game is run inside a giant 3D model of a tavern. Also flipping the table or throwing minis around is fun. Love it to death.

tl;dr: authentic as fuck. Buy if you like physics.

A small warning: don't play on Tuesday. The game goes through an update every Tuesday and it screws up the servers, making you disconnect constantly.

Tabletop Simulator is worth full price, I have already got over 170 hours on this game due to sheer amount of content it has that users have added. The workshop has all well known games and surprisingly a lot of niche games too. The community isn't toxic at all and a lot of people are always happy to explain games to new players. I find the interface very easy to use, the controls are intuitive and it doesn't feel like you're playing a video game necessarily.
I would give TTS a 9/10, the only thing I would change is making it easier to create workshop content but as I don't make things it doesn't affect me but I know a lot of people would like it to be more accessible.
I highly recommend buying this game especially in lockdown where you can move game sessions to online.
